:let, :body {:op :do, :ann {}, :stmts ({:args ({:op :lit, :val "anfcensus", :ann {}} {:op :lit, :val "data->form", :ann {}} {:op :map, :pairs ([{:op :lit, :val :doc, :ann {}} {:op :lit, :val "Turn a DATA value back into the reader form that denotes it — the exact\n   inverse of `datum`.\n\n   A macro is a function from data to data: it receives the call's parts as\n   plain values and returns a new value that stands for the code to compile\n   next. That returned value has to be turned back into reader-form shape so\n   the compiler can lower it. This walks the value and rebuilds nodes:\n     * a symbol node (already form-shaped) passes straight through;\n     * a metadata wrapper `{:meta form m}` keeps its wrapper, rebuilding the\n       form inside — a nil metadata is dropped (the bare form);\n     * a beam-lisp vector becomes a `:vector` node; if it carries author\n       metadata that metadata is re-wrapped so a later compile puts it back\n       onto the value, exactly as Clojure preserves `^{...}` on returned data;\n     * a set becomes a `:set` node, a list becomes a `:list` node;\n     * a plain map becomes a `:map` node of rebuilt key/value pairs;\n     * an atom that is not nil/true/false becomes a `:keyword` node;\n     * any other literal (number, string, boolean, nil) is already itself.", :ann {}}] [{:op :lit, :val :private, :ann {}} {:op :lit, :val true, :ann {}}]), :ann {}}), :mod :Elixir.BeamLisp.Env, :op :remote, :fun :put_meta, :ann {}} {:name "value", :op :var, :ann {}})}, :ann {}}
